data.name: Chandresh
data.gender_notes: Chandresh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'Chandra' meaning moon and 'Rish' meaning god. This name represents the grace and blessings of the Moon God. The name Chandresh carries the meaning “Moon God's Grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chandresh usually hope their child will grow to embody moon god's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chandresh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon God's Grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chandresh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Ravi is a popular Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit word meaning "sun". This name is associated with warmth, vitality, and the symbolism of the sun as a giver of life and energy.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the sun represents the deity Surya, who is believed to bring light, life, and knowledge to the world. This name signifies a deep connection to the divine and the power of the sun to illuminate one's path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chandresh, meaning 'moon among the masses', signifies enlightenment and leadership. The moon symbolizes the illumination of the mind, while 'among the masses' signifies guiding others towards wisdom and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Chandrashokasena was a king of the Sena dynasty, who ruled over present-day West Bengal and Bihar in India during the 12th and 13th centuries.
Chandragupta Maurya was a legendary emperor of ancient India, who is traditionally considered to have founded the Maurya Empire in 321 BC and ruled until 298 BC.

This name, meaning 'moon' or 'moon-lit' in Sanskrit, can be seen on various social media platforms used by individuals of Indian descent living abroad. The trend of Indian-origin names gaining popularity in the Western world is attributed to increasing multiculturalism and globalization. This name is also used by individuals who identify with their cultural roots and want to showcase their heritage on these platforms.
